positive_feedback: Grammar quality: parse_optimization_log_block/_entry_fields/_field/_record_value implement the closed EBNF exactly (§1.3a). Recovery is genuinely report-ALL, not bail-on-first: recover_to_optlog_boundary/recover_to_comma_or_rbrace are brace-depth-aware, correctly skipping over an inner `{...}` in a malformed value (e.g. the AT-2919 nested-record reject fixture) instead of mistaking it for the enclosing block's terminator -- a real, non-trivial recovery-correctness detail that a naive implementation would get wrong.

RecordValue integration is exactly as pinned: `AnnotationArg::Record{fields}` (block-level, direct) / `Call{"entry",[Record]}` (per-entry) with a genuinely closed `RecordValue{Str|Int|Ident}` -- no Record/Call/Hole variant, so nested records/calls/holes are structurally unrepresentable, not just runtime-rejected. Verified call-as-value and hole-as-value are each rejected with a precise, field-scoped error message before a `RecordValue` is ever produced.

opt_log.rs schema is clean and readable: OptLogUnit/OptLogVerdict as closed enums with from_ident/as_ident round-trip pairs, allows_negative() centralizing the per-unit sign rule instead of scattering it, validate_block/validate_entry separated exactly per the spec's threaded-version signature. Doc comments correctly and precisely distinguish the two forward_unknown reachability directions (block-level dead-by-EBNF-construction vs. entry-level live) -- this same distinction is carried faithfully into DESIGN.md and the coder's known_limitations, so the honest caveat propagates consistently across all three surfaces instead of drifting.

Writer splice mechanics are sound: span-based `close_brace_pos = ann.span.end - 1` with a debug_assert pinning the byte really is `}`, comma-insertion logic (`block_ends_with_comma_or_is_empty`) correctly handles empty-block/trailing-comma/normal cases without double-commas, and the whole splice function is Err-only-then-no-write (never a partial write) -- `append_optimization_log` only calls `std::fs::write` after `splice_optimization_log_entry` returns `Ok`. AT-2906's byte-preservation tests and my own read of the code agree the mechanism is a genuine surgical splice, not a reparse-reformat.

The QA-fix commit (a11f400) is exactly the right shape: fail-closed check added to the ONE shared core (`splice_optimization_log_entry`) so CLI and MCP inherit it for free (confirmed: MCP's `log_opt_error_to_mcp` routes every non-Io LogOptError, including the new UnsupportedVersion, through the same InvalidParams mapping -- no parallel reimplementation), ordered correctly (after the malformed-block check, before the capacity check), a distinct exit code (5) that doesn't collide with Full(3)/Multikernel(4)/generic(2), and the coder's self-report honestly retracts the disproven claim rather than papering over it. AT-2926's three tests (refuse+byte-unchanged in-memory, refuse+byte-unchanged on-disk, v1-still-works no-regression companion) cover exactly the QA-identified gap.

MCP tool #8 (append_optimization_log.rs) is idiomatic and thin as specified: a Deserialize request / Serialize response pair, validation via the existing from_ident closed-set parsers, a single delegate call into log_opt::append_optimization_log, and an honest doc comment explaining why --from-verify/--from-grid ingestion is deliberately NOT mirrored at the MCP layer (an MCP caller already holds the verdict/metric in-process; re-serializing to re-ingest would be pure overhead). AT-2912 is tested both at the handler level (this file) and at the process-boundary level (tests/mcp_roundtrip.rs), which is the right belt-and-suspenders split.

The carrier-shape decision is documented in exactly the three places the spec asked for (ast.rs Record doc comment, lower.rs lower_optimization_log_annotation doc comment, opt_log.rs module doc comment) and the three descriptions are mutually consistent -- no drift between them.

DESIGN.md §3.1.43 and both ROADMAP.md rows (FG.2 NO-BUILD / FG.3 IMPLEMENTED) are accurate against the diff: unit/verdict vocabularies, exit codes, AT ranges, and the forward_unknown block-vs-entry reachability caveat all match the code. Numbering verified correct (next-sequential after the real §3.1.42, not the r1 §3.1.44 slip).

minor_issues.description: FG.3's effort line reads '~500 LOC (spec estimate) -> ~950 LOC actual'. This number was written in the original feat commit (6c7732d) and was NOT revisited by the QA-fix commit (a11f400 touches only cli.rs/log_opt.rs/main.rs) or by the coder's corrected loc_budget_disclosure in M3.19-coder.json, which now honestly states the measured total is 3223 added lines (1902 production / 1277 test / 44 fixture) -- roughly 2x-3x higher than the '~950' figure this doc-facing row still shows. The '~950' appears to derive from the milestone spec's own §6 pre-implementation estimate ('push the honest cap to ~950'), not a post-hoc measurement, and was never corrected to match reality once QA measured it. Recommend a follow-up edit to ROADMAP.md's FG.3 row (or a note in §3.1.43) reconciling it with the coder's disclosed 3223/1902 figures, so a future reader isn't misled by the doc while the run JSON tells the true story. Not blocking -- QA already logged the underlying overrun as SHOULD-FIX/non-blocking and the coder's self-report is honest about it; this is purely a doc-sync gap between the run JSON and the checked-in prose.

In `at_2906_append_preserves_bytes_outside_spliced_region`, the `close` variable is computed via `src.rfind('}')` and then immediately discarded (`let _ = close;`) with a comment admitting the ambiguity ('use kernel's structure instead'). The test still passes and does assert real preservation via a weaker `contains(...)` check, but the dead computation plus the comment reads as an abandoned assertion attempt left in place. Cosmetic only -- worth a follow-up cleanup pass, not a re-submission trigger.

summary: FG.3 (@optimization_log minimal-build) is implemented exactly to the r2 spec: the closed RecordValue grammar, report-ALL parser recovery with correct brace-depth-aware re-sync, the version/forward-compat dual-mode validator, the byte-preserving splice writer with fail-closed capacity/multikernel/(post-QA-fix)version-mismatch guards, and the thin MCP wrapper are all present, correctly wired end-to-end (parser -> AST -> HIR -> writer -> MCP), and independently re-verified here (clean build, 576/576 tests passing across the three touched crates, zero clippy findings, clean git status). FG.2 (@transfer) is a genuine NO-BUILD -- zero parser/AST/HIR/codegen change, current-state anchored at AT-2915, revisit trigger recorded verbatim in both DESIGN.md and ROADMAP.md. The QA-blocking deviation-2 gap (writer silently splicing into an unreachable-by-false-premise version>1 block) is cleanly fixed in the shared splice core with an honest self-report retraction, not just a patch over the symptom. Two non-blocking findings: ROADMAP.md's FG.3 effort line ('~950 LOC actual') was not updated to match the coder's own corrected loc_budget_disclosure (measured 3223/1902), and one test file has a small dead-code/abandoned-assertion cosmetic wart. Neither affects correctness, spec compliance, or the codegen-inert safety gate. APPROVE.
